ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AD = 3$, $AB = 4$. Let $M$ be a moving point on line segment $BD$. Let $MP \perp CD$ at point $P$, and $MQ \perp BC$ at point $Q$. What is the minimum value of $PQ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect CM as shown in the diagram:
\[
\because \text{MP} \perp \text{CD at point P, MQ} \perp \text{BC at point Q,}
\]
\[
\therefore \angle \text{CPM} = \angle \text{CQM} = 90^\circ,
\]
\[
\because \text{Quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,}
\]
\[
\therefore \text{BC} = \text{AD} = 3, \text{CD} = \text{AB} = 4, \angle \text{BCD} = 90^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle \text{CPM} = \angle \text{CQM} = \angle \text{BCD} = 90^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \text{Quadrilateral PCQM is a rectangle,}
\]
\[
\therefore \text{PQ} = \text{CM},
\]
\[
\therefore \text{When CM is at its minimum, PQ is also at its minimum,}
\]
\[
\because \text{Point M moves along BD,}
\]
\[
\therefore \text{When CM} \perp \text{BD, CM is at its minimum, then PQ is at its minimum,}
\]
Using the Pythagorean theorem, we get:
\[
\text{BD} = \sqrt{\text{DC}^2 + \text{BC}^2} = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5,
\]
\[
\because {S}_{\triangle \text{BCD}} = \frac{1}{2} \text{BC} \times \text{CD} = \frac{1}{2} \text{BD} \times \text{CM},
\]
\[
\therefore \text{At this moment, CM} = \frac{\text{BC} \times \text{CD}}{\text{BD}} = \frac{3 \times 4}{5} = \boxed{\frac{12}{5}},
\]
\[
\therefore \text{The minimum value of PQ is} \frac{12}{5}.
\]

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangle ABCD, with D at the upper left, C at the upper right, A at the lower left, and B at the lower right. Segment DB is the diagonal from the upper left to the lower right, and point M is located on segment DB. Point P is on the upper side CD, and MP is vertical upward and perpendicular to CD; point Q is on the right side BC, and MQ is horizontal to the right and perpendicular to BC. The figure also draws the segment from P to Q, as well as the segment from C to M. Reasoning: Because MP ⟂ CD, MQ ⟂ BC, and in rectangle ABCD, CD ⟂ BC, the four angles of quadrilateral PCQM are all right angles, so it is a rectangle. The two diagonals of rectangle PCQM are equal, therefore PQ = CM. Thus asking for the minimum value of PQ is equivalent to asking for the minimum value of the distance CM from the fixed point C to M when point M moves on segment BD. The shortest distance from a point to a segment is obtained at the foot of the perpendicular; in right triangle BCD, when drawing a perpendicular from the right-angle vertex C to the hypotenuse BD, CM is minimal. Given in the problem AD = 3, AB = 4, and opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so BC = 3 and CD = 4. In right triangle BCD, BD = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5. Using equality of areas: the area of triangle BCD is both equal to (1/2)·BC·CD = (1/2)·3·4, and equal to (1/2)·BD·CM_min = (1/2)·5·CM_min. Therefore CM_min = 3·4/5 = 12/5. Since PQ = CM, the minimum value of PQ is 12/5.
